summary: Mark Teeuwen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who earned his MA (~1984–1989) and Ph.D. (~1990–1996) from Leiden University. He served as a lecturer at Cardiff University (1994–1999) before becoming a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.

Mark Wilks was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Resident at the Kingdom of Mysore (~1803–1808), Governor of Saint Helena (~1813–1816), and was made a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1826.
Mark William Carr was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Assistant Inspector General for the Madras Police in 1862 and as a Major in the Madras Staff Corps in 1870.
Mark Zebrowski was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Dartmouth College (~1961–1965) and Harvard University (~1965–1969).

Markus Gabriel, a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn (~2000–2002), has held posts at Heidelberg, The New School, and Bonn (Professor 2009, Director 2012 and 2017). Later appointments include The New Institute (2022–2024), Kyoto Institute of Philosophy (2024), and Kyoto University (2026).

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna (-2012) under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He has worked as a project researcher at Heidelberg University and holds a faculty post at Vienna (attested 2026).

Marsha Weidner is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley. She served as an assistant professor of art history at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and Professor of the History of Art at the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Marshall Livingston Perrin was a linguist who studied at Harvard and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen (1883–1889). He taught at Göttingen (1885–1888) and Boston University, where he was Assistant Professor (1888–1891) and became Professor of Sanskrit in 1910.

Marshall Sahlins was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1948–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954), later holding posts at Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (1973).
Marta Bianco is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. She earned two master's degrees (-2023, -2025) at the University of Naples "L'Orientale," where she became a PhD candidate in 2024.

Marta Sanvido is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She held positions at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2019–2020), UC Berkeley (2021–2023), and the University of Hamburg (2023–2024), before becoming Assistant Professor at Yale University in 2025.

Marta Sernesi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Turin in 2007 and was attested as a Gastprofessorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Martha A. Muusses was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned her Ph.D. under Willem Caland at Utrecht University (-1920) and studied at Uppsala (1926). She worked at the Batavian Society of Arts and Sciences (1921–1926) and taught Dutch at Copenhagen, Stockholm, Uppsala, and Gothenburg.

Martha Ann Selby is an Indologist who served as Series Editor for South Asia Research (attested 2014). She is a Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin and serves as the Sangam Professor of South Asian Studies and Department Chair at Harvard University (attested 2026).
Martha Lile Love was an Indologist who completed her B.A. at the University of Toronto (~1968–1972) and pursued further studies at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at Wellesley, NYU, and Harvard, also studying under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Harvard, Oxford, and Brown before becoming Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor of Law and Ethics at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Martin Baumann is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leibniz University Hannover (~1989–1993) and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig (~1994–1999) before becoming Professor of Religious Studies and seminar director at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under several traditional teachers, Delhi University, and the University of Zurich (doctorate ~1970–1976). He held leadership and curatorial posts at Zurich's Ethnographic Museum from 1975 and was Chief Curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt is a historian of Japan and Buddhism who studied at Cambridge and Harvard (Ph.D. 1969–1975). He taught at Yokohama National University and the University of Tokyo (1963–1969) and directed Princeton University's East Asian Studies Program (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (-2002) under Lambert Schmithausen and studied at Kyoto University. His academic posts include Hamburg, the University of Göttingen, Ryukoku University, Shandong University (2019), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
